asi.hypothesis: The baseline will confirm that client-side N+1 user-composition requests and poster transfers dominate visual readiness.
asi.finding: The homepage issued 46 user-composition API requests and transferred 18.2 MB before visual readiness; LCP nearly equals visualReadyMs, while initial HTML and hydration finished under 100 ms.
asi.next_action_hint: Return card-ready metadata in the list response so the homepage does not fetch 45 full Presets individually.

description: Eliminate homepage N+1 full-Preset fetches by returning card metadata in the local list response

asi.hypothesis: Deriving poster key, duration, and surface type while the local server already parses each composition will remove 45 redundant browser requests and reduce client work without caching changing Presets.
asi.finding: User-composition requests fell from 46 to 1 and visual readiness improved by 199 ms (12.9%). The 18.1 MB transfer remains almost entirely poster imagery, and LCP still determines readiness.
asi.user_constraint: Presets are frequently changing local data; hard caching and hardcoded metadata are not acceptable. Continue targeting JavaScript, Svelte rendering, and request scheduling.
asi.next_action_hint: Profile why the browser transfers roughly the entire 15 MB poster corpus on the initial viewport despite lazy loading; fix Svelte/DOM image scheduling rather than caching data.

description: Gate poster image creation with a near-viewport IntersectionObserver attachment

asi.hypothesis: Explicitly mounting only near-viewport images will avoid native lazy-loading's broad preload distance and reduce contention from the dense grid.
asi.finding: LCP improved by 28 ms versus the current best, but overall visual readiness regressed by 43 ms and transfer size barely changed. Chrome still requested nearly the full poster corpus, likely because the first 45-card user section remains within the observer scheduling/layout window or because readiness/network accounting captures subsequent observer intersections.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric worsened by 3.2% versus the current best; added observer complexity did not materially reduce transferred bytes.
asi.next_action_hint: Profile request initiators and poster dimensions/count rather than adding another lazy-load layer. Investigate duplicate full-resolution poster decodes and whether responsive thumbnail generation is the actual bottleneck.

description: Defer poster alpha-crop scans until browser idle so decoded images can paint first

asi.hypothesis: Synchronous per-image alpha scans in load handlers delay Svelte's ready-state paint during a burst of local poster decodes.
asi.finding: The benchmark improved another 70 ms versus the current best and showed only 540 KB of poster data; 18.6 MB total is mostly dev-server script/module overhead. Correctness checks failed without surfaced output because checks.sh suppresses stdout, so the promising change was reverted.
asi.rollback_reason: Required npm check failed; a benchmark improvement cannot be kept with failed checks.
asi.next_action_hint: Reapply the idle crop change, run npm check directly to expose and fix the type/compiler error, then rerun. Improve checks.sh so failure output is visible.

description: Move non-critical poster alpha-crop scans out of image load handlers and into browser idle time

asi.hypothesis: Synchronous alpha-crop work in each image load handler blocks Svelte ready-state paints even though the decoded poster is already usable.
asi.finding: Deferring crop refinement improved visual readiness by 48 ms versus the current best and improved LCP by 280 ms. Poster traffic is only 45 requests/540 KB; cold dev-server JavaScript/module traffic is the larger remaining cost.
asi.next_action_hint: Reduce homepage client module graph. The page imports the full preset engine module, eagerly validates 99 JSON files, and pulls editor/runtime dependencies just to render the library.

description: Render the dynamic Preset catalog from server-derived card metadata and lazy-load editor-only modules on user actions

asi.hypothesis: The homepage should not import and validate the full frequently changing Preset corpus or editor/runtime modules merely to render card labels and thumbnails.
asi.finding: Visual readiness improved by 358 ms versus the current best and 605 ms versus baseline. Initial script traffic fell from 6.29 MB to 1.86 MB, preset module traffic fell from 1.12 MB to zero, and total cold dev-server traffic fell by 7.6 MB. Metadata remains derived from live Presets on every server module refresh; nothing is hardcoded or persistently cached.
asi.next_action_hint: Remove the remaining post-mount user-composition list fetch by including server-derived user card metadata in page data, so user cards and poster requests can begin in SSR without a second render.

description: Move user-composition card metadata into homepage SSR through a shared server catalog

asi.hypothesis: Server-rendering user cards will remove the post-mount list request and let visible posters begin sooner.
asi.finding: The API request disappeared, LCP improved 24 ms, and only 26 posters were requested, but sequentially reading, validating, and inspecting 45 user compositions increased TTFB by 38 ms and overall visual readiness regressed 127 ms.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric worsened 13.6% versus the current best. Moving existing sequential work onto the critical server path was counterproductive.
asi.next_action_hint: If revisiting SSR user cards, first make server catalog reads concurrent and provide a card-only lane that does not perform media inspection unused by the homepage. Otherwise keep the client request off the initial critical path.

description: Read and inspect local user-composition metadata concurrently in the collection endpoint

asi.hypothesis: Parallel local file reads and media inspections will shorten the post-mount user-composition request.
asi.finding: The run regressed 129 ms, driven by unrelated-looking initial navigation TTFB growth from 35 ms to 86 ms; API request count and payload were unchanged. Concurrency did not produce a measurable end-to-end win under the primary workload.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric worsened 13.9% versus the current best; do not retain concurrency solely on an unproven micro-optimization.
asi.next_action_hint: Focus on initial render and image priority. Add phase signal for the user-composition response before retrying server endpoint changes.

description: Replace non-reactive poster crop cache SvelteMap with a plain Map

asi.hypothesis: The module cache has no reactive consumers, so a plain Map may avoid unnecessary Svelte invalidation overhead during image-load bursts.
asi.finding: ESLint requires SvelteMap for mutable Maps in components, and the benchmark was substantially worse. The run also had unusually high TTFB/load timing, but there is no evidence this change helps.
asi.rollback_reason: Correctness checks failed on svelte/prefer-svelte-reactivity and primary metric regressed.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep SvelteMap to satisfy project lint. Profile reactive invalidation with tooling before challenging the rule.

description: Add user-composition response timing and confirm the optimized homepage on a repeated cold-browser run

asi.hypothesis: A repeated run with explicit API response timing will separate dev-server variance from user-composition and poster phases.
asi.finding: Unchanged product code measured 810 ms, 123 ms faster than the prior keep, confirming substantial warm dev-server variance. User metadata finished at 379 ms; visible poster/LCP completion followed about 417 ms later. Treat small future differences cautiously and target structural changes larger than this noise.
asi.next_action_hint: Optimize the 379–796 ms image/decode/render phase. Test removing the decorative 300 ms opacity fade, which may delay LCP without helping skeleton readiness.

description: Mount poster images only when their previews intersect the viewport

asi.hypothesis: A zero-margin IntersectionObserver will prevent native lazy loading from prefetching off-screen rows while preserving dynamic poster behavior.
asi.finding: Poster requests fell from 45 to 23, poster bytes fell 43%, and LCP improved 228 ms, but the primary metric was 1.6 ms worse than the current best—well within observed dev-server noise.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric did not improve, and the added attachment should not be kept based only on secondary metrics without confirmation.
asi.next_action_hint: Repeat the exact candidate once as advised for a within-noise result; keep only if primary improvement confirms while request/LCP gains persist.

description: Load dynamic posters only when their card previews actually enter the viewport

asi.hypothesis: Repeating the zero-margin viewport attachment will confirm whether its near-neutral first primary result was noise while preserving large LCP/request reductions.
asi.finding: Confirmed: visual readiness improved 52 ms versus the current best, LCP improved another 296 ms, poster requests fell from 45 to 14, and poster bytes fell 64%. Off-screen dynamic posters still load when scrolled into view; no content or cache is hardcoded.
asi.next_action_hint: The user-composition response now ends around 366 ms and LCP around 500 ms. Investigate whether returning a card-only response can reduce API parse/media inspection without moving work into TTFB.

description: Add a card-only user-composition response that skips media inspection unused by the homepage

asi.hypothesis: The homepage card lane can preserve schema and semantic validation while skipping media filesystem inspection and response fields it never reads.
asi.finding: Visual readiness improved 16.6 ms, API response end improved 16.4 ms, and LCP improved 24 ms. The card response remains derived from each current local Preset and validates it; this is not caching or hardcoding.
asi.next_action_hint: Add focused coverage for the card view contract, then test whether the remaining 300 ms image opacity transition affects perceived readiness or only LCP.

description: Mark observer-confirmed visible posters as high fetch priority

asi.hypothesis: Once IntersectionObserver confirms a poster is visible, high fetch priority may finish its local request and decode sooner.
asi.finding: Primary metric regressed 2.7 ms and LCP regressed 8 ms; the run also requested 23 rather than 14 posters, suggesting priority provided no stable scheduling benefit.
asi.rollback_reason: No primary improvement and no secondary evidence of benefit.
asi.next_action_hint: Leave browser priority automatic. Use the final iteration for focused contract coverage and a confirmation run of the kept state.

asi.hypothesis: Explicit asynchronous decoding will keep visible poster decodes from blocking the main thread during Svelte's user-card insertion.
asi.finding: Visual readiness improved 18 ms versus the current best and LCP improved 8 ms. User API timing also varied lower, so the gain is modest but the primary metric improved with all checks passing.
asi.next_action_hint: Stop at the user-requested 15-run cap. Add focused card-view contract coverage during normal follow-up rather than another optimization experiment.

description: Preload the dynamic user-composition card response from homepage HTML

asi.hypothesis: Starting the same dynamic card-response fetch from the HTML head will overlap local Preset parsing with hydration and reduce the post-mount wait without caching or hardcoding data.
asi.finding: The card response ended only 9 ms earlier, while DOMContentLoaded regressed by about 390 ms and visual readiness regressed by 899 ms. Preloading the CPU-heavy local endpoint competed with critical dev-server module transformation and hydration rather than creating useful overlap.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric more than doubled; eager preload moved non-critical local parsing onto the critical path.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep user-composition loading after mount. Future work should reduce endpoint CPU cost or use true server streaming, not raise its network priority.

description: Read and validate local user compositions concurrently for the card endpoint

asi.hypothesis: Parallel filesystem reads will reduce the card endpoint's response time while retaining full schema and semantic validation of frequently changing local Presets.
asi.finding: The user-composition response ended 9 ms later than the current best, LCP regressed 40 ms, and visual readiness regressed 23 ms. Concurrent reads did not help because validation and hashing remain CPU-bound on the single JavaScript thread, while extra promise scheduling added overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric worsened 3.2% and the endpoint-specific timing also regressed.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep sequential reads. A meaningful endpoint improvement requires reducing repeated CPU validation/hashing work through an invalidation-safe design, not parallelizing local I/O.

description: Load Graffiti only on the workspace route instead of the homepage layout

asi.hypothesis: The homepage fully restyles its controls and should not load the workspace-oriented Graffiti package globally; route-scoping it may shrink cold dev-server work without changing workspace behavior.
asi.finding: Total response traffic fell by about 361 KB, confirming Graffiti contributed avoidable homepage bytes, but visual readiness regressed 40 ms, LCP regressed 40 ms, and the user API completed 59 ms later. The byte reduction did not translate into the primary metric under this workload.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric worsened 5.6%; do not retain a dependency-boundary refactor based only on transferred bytes.
asi.next_action_hint: Profile the client main-thread timeline or endpoint CPU directly before another structural change. Remaining differences are now close to dev-server variance.
